To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) young and older adults differ in the extent to which they produce mental imagery during the learning of words and (2) the concreteness effect in memory for words is greater for young adults than for older adults when they are explicitly instructed to form mental images of the words.

the concreteness effect is greater for young subjects than for elderly subjects when imagery is explicitly instructed and that this age-related difference in the concreteness advantage is mediated by age-related differences in imagery production.

(1) young subjects benefit more from imagery than do older ones, (2) older subjects benefit more from concrete than from abstract words, (3) this advantage of concrete over abstraction words for older subjects reflects the use of imagery, and (4) the concreteness effect for older subjects is greater under imagery instructions than under verbal instructions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of age on the utilization of visual imagery as a mnemonic strategy.
the effects of imagery processing on the concreteness effect.
the effects of age-related differences in imagery processing on the concreteness effect and on subsequent memory performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
imagery processing is not an effective strategy for young or elderly subjects in the recall of abstract words.
the effects of age on memory are not a function of the use of imagery but are a function of the type of imagery used, i.e., the type of imagery processing.
the effects of aging on memory are a function of the processing of information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
imagery production and use are not necessarily related to recall performance, but that they are related when the material to be recalled is concrete.
the concreteness effect is a function of the degree of imagery production.
imagery is a useful mnemonic device for younger adults but is not so effective for older adults, and that the concreteness effect in recall may be due to the use of imagery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
imagery is an important component of memory and that the use of imagery may be particularly important in the elderly.
older adults are not only more susceptible to the effects of imagery on memory but that they are also more likely to use it.
imagery plays a key role in memory, and it is important to consider the effects of aging on the use of imagery in memory.
